title: LCLI-690 review minors: the schema-regeneration handshake line is unconditional, and a dropped type leaves an unwarned orphaned schema
description:
Three MINOR findings from the LCLI-690 review, filed so they can be picked up (a gap that lives only in a closed record summary is durable but nobody can act on it). None is fixed here and none blocks anything. NOT CAMPAIGN WORK.

F3 — docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md, section "3. Cut a release", the LCLI-469 first-message paragraph (~L801-804): "The bump is not baseline-only: the same change must also regenerate the consumer's committed OKF schemas, with `lore schema export` run under the new lore version ... or their `lore check` goes red with exit 6." It states the schema regeneration UNCONDITIONALLY. It is needed only when the release changes schema-affecting inputs (a document type added, removed or changed, moving the profile digest — LCLI-690's own case was a new Standard type). A release whose OKF schema surface is unchanged needs no regeneration, and the sentence should say so.

F4 — the section-3 sentence above carries no test guard. The post-latest checklist block scripts/promote-latest.mjs prints IS guarded: test/promote-latest.test.ts's "the runbook item it cites carries the same five steps" test reads release-publishing.md section 3 item 8 (POST_LATEST_RUNBOOK_ITEM, scripts/promote-latest.mjs:1149) and asserts it contains "lore schema export". The section-3 first-message sentence sits outside that item, so a future edit can drop it silently.

Open edge — a release that DROPS a type leaves the consumer's committed schema for that type orphaned, and nothing warns. The committed file carries the PREVIOUS profile's x-lore-generator.profileDigest, so the new binary reads it as `schema-unattributable` and exits 7 (indeterminate); `lore schema export` does NOT prune it — a full export KEEPS an unattributable orphan and warns only on stderr OUTSIDE --json (test/schema-drift.test.ts:306-331, test/schema-export.test.ts:277-305). Neither the runbook text nor the printed checklist says a dropped type leaves this orphan, so a consumer following the handshake can be left with a persistent exit-7 finding they were never told about.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md section 3 states that schema regeneration is needed only when the release changes schema-affecting inputs, not unconditionally, and a test guard covers that section-3 sentence as well as the post-latest checklist item it already covers
A dropped type's orphaned committed schema is warned about where the handshake is described (runbook text and/or the printed checklist), so a consumer is not left with an unexplained exit 7
